title: zazzled features
description: Behavior the daemon adds to the commands' answers: session ids and dedupe, read-again, and stored outputs.

entities.name: Session ids and dedupe
entities.description: Within a session, each query answer has a short id, and an answer already sent recently is replaced by a one-line notice.
entities.behavior: When a request carries a session (ZAZZLE_SESSION through the invoker or `zazzled run`; one random `mcp-...` id per `zazzled mcp` process), a find, read, ls, outline or refs answer starts with `[r:ID]`, ID being at least five characters derived from a hash of the session and the text. If the same session was sent the identical text within its last 40,000 estimated tokens, the answer is `[r:ID] already sent: zazzle CMD ARGS, unchanged. If you no longer have it: read-again r:ID`. --disable-session-deduping (MCP disable_session_deduping) sends it in full again.
entities.outcome: An agent is not sent text that is still in its context, and can refer to earlier answers by id.
constraints: No session, no ids and no dedupe.
Edits, errors, status, help and version are never given an id or deduplicated; clean, `zazzle run` and proxied outputs get no session id either, but an output id of their own (stored-outputs).
Sessions live in daemon memory only; a restart forgets them.
At most 64 sessions (the least recently used is dropped) and 512 answers per session (the oldest is dropped).

entities.name: Read again by id
entities.description: An answer can be fetched again by its id: a session response unchanged under the same id or current under a new one; a stored output as it was shown, or in full.
entities.behavior: With each id the session table keeps the command line (without --disable-session-deduping) and working directory that produced it. `zazzle read-again r:ID` (MCP zazzle_read_again) runs that request again in its original working directory and session: if the text is the same, it comes back whole under the same id; if not, it comes back under a new id with `r:OLD changed since it was sent; this is the current version`. A read again never reveals more than the original request did: a terse view stays without a sha. An id the session does not hold (or any id, without a session) is looked up in the output store instead: a stored clean, run or proxy output comes back as it was shown, and with --full (or --lines A-B) its whole input comes back as numbered lines within a budget of 3000 tokens (--budget).
entities.outcome: An agent can drop an answer from its context, or lose it to compaction, keep only its id, and get it back exactly when needed.
constraints: A session response is rerun only within its session, and only while the session table keeps it (512 per session, daemon memory only).
A stored output is there for an hour at most (stored-outputs); --full is refused for a session response, which is never cut.

entities.name: Stored outputs
entities.description: clean, `zazzle run` and proxied outputs, whose input cannot be had again, are kept for an hour under an id, with the input they came from.
entities.behavior: When clean (in the daemon or `zazzled run`), `zazzled wrap` or `zazzled proxy` has an output store, it saves the text it shows and its whole input under a ten-character id derived from both. clean and run answers start with `[r:ID]`, and end with `[full output: read-again r:ID --full]` when something was cut: input past its cap, a budget, a run profile's dropped lines, progress bars, blobs or long lines. The proxy appends to the result, after its items, one item of its own per text it shortened, `[r:ID shortened by zazzle]` (with `; full text: read-again r:ID --full` when something was cut), so a JSON text stays JSON. `read-again r:ID` returns the output as shown; `--full` returns the input with its line numbers. Each save drops entries older than an hour and, past the size limit, the oldest until half the bytes remain.
entities.outcome: An agent can drop a cleaned output from its context, or see what cleaning cut, without running a build or test again or asking the other server again.
constraints: Kept for an hour at most, and less when the store passes its size limit (ZAZZLE_OUTPUTS_MAX_GB, default 2).
The store is the directory each process finds in its own environment (ZAZZLE_OUTPUTS_DIR, else ~/.zazzle/outputs); a `zazzle run` or proxy output is found only by a daemon using the same one.
Without HOME or ZAZZLE_OUTPUTS_DIR nothing is stored and outputs carry no id; a save that fails leaves the output with a note that it was not stored.

entities.name: Routing hook for Claude Code and Codex
entities.description: `zazzled hook --client claude-code|codex [--edits]` is the PreToolUse hook setup installs: it refuses raw shell searches, listings, reads and builds with a pointer to the zazzle tool or `zazzle run`, and logs what it lets through.

sources.symbol: Routing: what is enforced and what is asked

entities.behavior: It reads the hook payload on stdin. Shell commands (Claude Code's Bash, Codex's shell, including `bash -lc` scripts) are split into pipeline segments; a segment that runs grep, rg, ag, ack or git grep, find without actions, cat/head/tail/less/bat/nl on files, sed -n on files, or a build or test runner (cargo build/test/check/clippy, dotnet build/test, go build/test, npm/pnpm/yarn/bun test/run/install, make, pytest, gradle, mvn, tsc, jest, vitest, xcodebuild and others) is refused with `permissionDecision: deny` and the zazzle tool or `zazzle run --` to use instead. Claude Code's Grep and Glob are refused, Read only for .cs files. Edit tools (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, apply_patch) are allowed and logged as native edits, or refused with --edits (which also refuses Read). A command ending in `# allow-raw` passes and is logged; when the zazzle daemon cannot be reached every refusal becomes a logged pass; ZAZZLE_HOOK=off turns it off. It never rewrites or approves a command.
entities.outcome: Raw tool calls that zazzle can answer more cheaply are sent back to the agent with the zazzle equivalent, in both Claude Code and Codex, and every bypass is visible in the activity log.
constraints: Codex runs a new or changed hook only after the user trusts it.
Claude Code's Read of non-C# files is allowed, since its Edit tool needs it.
Hosted tools, web tools and MCP servers left direct are not seen.

entities.name: Workspace boundaries for edits
entities.description: Edits may write in the working directory, the git work tree holding it, the roots the MCP client names and the user's workspaces, and nowhere else.
entities.behavior: workspace::roots collects the command's working directory and its git work tree (so a chat started in a subdirectory edits the whole repository), the roots an MCP client returns for roots/list (asked after initialize when the client offers roots, and again on roots/list_changed, carried to the daemon after the session id), and the folders in ~/.zazzle/workspaces (one per line, `~/` allowed, written by `zazzle setup --workspace`) and ZAZZLE_WORKSPACES. The home folder and / never count, so a chat started there edits only its workspaces. confine resolves symlinks and `..` and refuses anything outside, naming the allowed folders and how to add one.
entities.outcome: One global setup lets an agent edit any repository under ~/dev from a chat started anywhere, including by absolute path and across repositories, without unrestricted writes.
constraints: A linked git worktree outside every workspace is refused until its folder is added.

entities.name: Activity log
entities.description: Every zazzle command the daemon runs, every `zazzle run`, every tool call through the proxy and every hook decision other than a plain allow is appended to ~/.zazzle/activity.log as one JSON line.
entities.behavior: Entries carry the time, the source (zazzle, run, proxy, hook), the session, the folder and what ran with its status or outcome; the proxy adds the server it fronts. version and status calls are left out. The log is moved to activity.log.1 past 2 MiB; ZAZZLE_ACTIVITY_LOG moves it, an empty value turns it off. Failures to write are ignored.
entities.outcome: `zazzle setup --report` and `--verify` can show what actually went through zazzle and what bypassed it, instead of inferring coverage from configuration.
constraints: Tool calls that never reach zazzle (native tools the hook allows, direct MCP servers) leave no entry.

entities.name: Small fixed cost per agent session
entities.description: What an agent pays for zazzle before and around its work is kept small: short MCP instructions, a catalog without the zazz tools until a script is registered, one shared budget for a multi-path read, similar files offered for a missing path, and one immediate message while the C# indexer is unavailable, sent in full once per session and shortened on repeats like an error's usage line and `similar:` list.
entities.behavior: Initialize sends about 500 characters of instructions (the full text stays in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md); tools/list has 13 tools unless ZAZZLE_MCP_ZAZZ=1 or a zazz script is registered; read gives each remaining path an even share of what is left of its budget and names files it did not reach; read, outline and ls add `similar: ...` with up to three files of the same name or stem; after a failed indexer connection, structure tools answer `C# indexer unavailable: WHY` at once for 15 s, and report_gap still records the gap in the activity log.
entities.outcome: Measured on this repository: instructions 2,044 to 524 characters, catalog 14,370 to 8,939 characters, a four-file read of 2,000-line files 39,137 to 10,358 bytes, and a Java test class outline from 1 symbol to 5 (class and its four methods). Repeated errors in one MCP session: the indexer-unavailable message 148 to 86 characters, a usage line to `usage: as above` (read's is 212 characters).
constraints: Clients that repeat the instructions per tool (Codex tool discovery) still pay them once per discovered tool.
Suggestions only search the work tree holding the working directory (or the working directory), and only by file name.
